content:
Ravi S: kicking off canary for Tidal-23B (int4). initial long-gen tests show fragmentation OOMs when requests exceed ~900 tokens.
Elena G: is batching configured differently from the onboarding template?
Ravi S: yes — max_batch_size=6, prefetch=on in template. failures mainly when batch>=3 + long gens.
Marcus K: please try max_batch_size=2 and default max_new_tokens=400 for canary.
Ravi S: local smoke: prefetch=false + batch=2 + default_max_new_tokens=400 -> ran 200 long-gen traces, 0 OOMs, tail latency ok.
qa-bot: eval-summary Tidal-23B-int4 vs float32: ROUGE-L -0.7%, QA EM -1.0% (within canary thresholds).
Elena G: router rule idea: if requested_max_new_tokens > 512 then route to pool "no-prefetch". keeps low-latency users on fast path.
deploy-bot: canary rollout: 2/4 pods updated.
Ravi S: logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-22T12:05:11Z] kv_alloc fail needed=1.1GiB total_free=900MiB largest_free=200MiB small_frag=0.56
[2026-03-22T12:05:11Z] OOM -> triggered compactor fast-pass reclaimed 640MiB
```
Marcus K: add metric frag_index = largest_free_block / total_free_mem. alert when frag_index < 0.35 for >5m.
Elena G: also add a nightly low-QPS long-gen job to exercise compactor and validate.
Ravi S: pushing PR canary/tidal-mem-safety with flags: per-request prefetch toggle, adaptive max_new_tokens, reduced concurrency. checklist + rollback criteria in PR.
Marcus K: if 24h stable, plan staged reserved rollout with slightly more conservative defaults.
Ravi S: tagging @oncall. will post 12h metrics and logs here. :thumbsup:
